claims.claim: Swish containment is exactly a multiplicity-respecting directed-cycle problem.
claims.evidence: After fixing one allowed orientation per selected physical card, direct an arc from its hoop to its ball. In a nonempty Swish every used vertex has indegree and outdegree exactly one, so every connected component is a directed simple cycle and the physical cards in any component are themselves a Swish. Conversely, distinct physical cards realizing a directed simple cycle place exactly one hoop and one ball at every cycle vertex. Requiring each type no more often than its physical multiplicity makes both directions exact.
claims.witness: The two-way construction maps any Swish component to its directed cycle and maps any multiplicity-feasible directed simple cycle back to a Swish.
claims.search_method: Independent proof from the source definition, explicitly tracking physical-card identities and allowed transformations.

claims.claim: The transformation action gives four position orbits, eight internal card types, and twenty-eight cross-orbit types in fourteen reversal pairs.
claims.evidence: The Klein-four action partitions the grid into orbits of sizes 4,2,4,2. The two free four-point orbits have three internal ordered-pair types each, while the two two-point orbits have one each, totaling eight. For AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD the directed cross-type counts are 2,4,2,2,2,2 in either direction, totaling 28. Reversal bijects the two directions and produces fourteen pairs.
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of all ordered pairs of distinct grid positions modulo the four allowed transformations, supplemented by orbit-stabilizer counting.

claims.claim: A no-swish collection contains at most 20 distinct transformation types, and this is sharp.
claims.evidence: Both types in any cross-orbit reversal pair realize a directed two-cycle, so at most one of each of fourteen pairs may occur. On each free four-point orbit, the three nonidentity translation types together realize a directed triangle, limiting support to two; each two-point orbit contributes at most its sole type. Hence support is at most 14+2+1+2+1=20. Taking every cross type forward in A<B<C<D and the six stated internal types is cycle-free, proving sharpness.
claims.witness: A 20-type witness consists of all fourteen forward cross types plus internal representatives (1,1)->(1,3), (1,1)->(4,1), (1,2)->(4,2), (2,1)->(2,3), (2,1)->(3,1), and (2,2)->(3,2).
claims.search_method: Derived all two-cycle and internal-triangle obstructions and independently checked the proposed extremal support under the exact transformation action.

claims.claim: Every 60-card once-or-twice model has a 28-card no-swish subset; unless all eight internal types are doubled, it has a 29-card no-swish subset.
claims.evidence: If the eight internal types have total multiplicity M0, the 60-M0 physical cross cards are forward in exactly half of the 24 orbit orders on average. Some order therefore has at least ceil((60-M0)/2) forward cards. Adding one copy of each of the six cycle-free internal seed types preserves acyclicity. Since M0<=16 this gives at least 28; if any internal type is not doubled, M0<=15 and it gives at least 29.
claims.witness: For an orbit order maximizing the forward count, select every physical cross card directed forward and add the six internal representatives from claim 2.
claims.search_method: Exact double counting over all 24 total orders, with integer ceiling thresholds and an independent acyclicity check of the six-card seed.

claims.claim: If a once-or-twice model has maximum no-swish size 28, then all eight internal types are doubled and the cross-card multiplicities are directionally balanced between every pair of position orbits.
claims.evidence: Claim 3 forces every internal type to be doubled. The remaining 44 cross cards give average forward count 22. If W_ij differs from W_ji, choose an order where i and j are adjacent and swap them; no other comparison changes, while the forward count changes by the nonzero difference. Thus the integer forward counts are nonconstant with average 22, so one is at least 23. Adding the six safe internal cards produces a 29-card no-swish subset, contradicting maximum 28.
claims.witness: The adjacent-swap pair of orbit orders is a constructive certificate that any directional imbalance yields an order with at least 23 forward cross cards.
claims.search_method: Proved the adjacent-swap argument and exhaustively checked all 148,578 feasible directional duplicate-count profiles with sixteen cross duplications.

claims.claim: When all eight internal types are doubled, any no-swish subset contains at most six internal cards.
claims.evidence: Every internal type is reversal-invariant, so selecting its two physical copies realizes opposite arcs and a two-card Swish. Thus at most one copy per internal type is usable. On each free four-point orbit, selecting all three internal types realizes a directed triangle, leaving at most two; the two smaller orbits contribute at most one each. The total is at most 2+1+2+1=6.
claims.witness: The six internal representatives used in claim 2 attain the bound with one card of each selected type.
claims.search_method: Enumerated all 3^8 internal submultisets and all simple-cycle type requirements within the four position orbits.

claims.claim: For a fixed unordered orbit pair with k reversal pairs and d doubled types in each direction, a no-swish subset contains at most k+d cards between those two orbits.
claims.evidence: A positive selection in both directions with the same quotient label gives a two-cycle, so at most k distinct labels contribute first copies. If selected second copies occur in both directions, choose their labels delta and epsilon; they must be distinct. The four arcs gH_i->gdelta H_j->gdeltaepsilon H_i->gepsilon H_j->gH_i use the two copies of each type. Distinctness modulo H_iH_j ensures the two vertices in each orbit are distinct, so this is a valid four-cycle. Hence bonuses can occur in only one direction, contributing at most its d doubled types, for a total at most k+d.
claims.witness: The displayed alternating four-cycle is a concrete obstruction whenever second-copy bonuses are selected in both directions under different labels.
claims.search_method: Reproved the quotient-label argument and exhaustively tested all 100 balanced local multiplicity assignments and 110,550 selected submultisets across all six orbit-pair geometries.

claims.claim: Under the once-or-twice model, maximum no-swish size is exactly 28 if and only if all eight internal types are doubled and W_ij=W_ji for every unordered position-orbit pair.
claims.evidence: Necessity follows from claims 3 and 4. For sufficiency, doubling all eight internal types leaves sixteen doubled cross types. Directional balance means each orbit pair has d_ij doubled types in either direction, with sum d_ij=8. Claim 6 bounds cross cards by sum(k_ij+d_ij)=14+8=22, and claim 5 bounds internal cards by six, giving an upper bound of 28. Claim 3 supplies a matching lower bound. If either stated condition fails, claims 3 or 4 supply 29 cards.
claims.witness: Any balanced model has a 28-card lower witness from the maximizing-order construction, while the independent local caps certify that no 29-card no-swish subset exists.
claims.search_method: Combined independently verified necessity and sufficiency bounds; also exhausted every feasible aggregate profile, finding 186 balanced and 148,392 unbalanced profiles with the predicted behavior.

claims.claim: The sealed source omits information essential to deciding the exact commercial-deck target, even though the once-or-twice abstract model now has an exact criterion.
claims.evidence: The authorized source states that the commercial deck has 60 cards and 36 symmetry types and records the open 28-versus-29 question, but provides neither the type multiplicity vector nor the internal duplication flags or directional totals needed by claim 7. This is outcome-relevant: the proposed Deck X is balanced and has maximum 28, whereas Deck Y has an explicitly cycle-free 29-card selection. Both have all 36 types, exactly 24 doubled types, and 60 cards, so the supplied aggregate facts do not distinguish the outcomes.
claims.witness: Deck X doubles all eight internal types and both directions of eight cross reversal pairs. Deck Y doubles all fourteen backward types, nine forward types, and one internal type; both copies of those nine forward types, one copy of the other five forward types, and the six safe internal cards form a 29-card no-swish subset.
claims.search_method: Inspected only the authorized source text for deck data and exactly reconstructed both abstract decks and the Deck Y witness.

target_evidence: The draft does not decide whether the actual commercial deck satisfies the balance criterion and does not exhibit a 29-card subset of that actual deck, so it does not fully resolve the exact source target. It nevertheless proves material, correct progress: a universal 28-card lower bound and an exact 28-versus-at-least-29 criterion for the explicit once-or-twice abstraction. Its express PARTIAL resolution claim is therefore accurate.
